title: Instance Specific Approximations for Unconstrained Submodular Maximization with Modular Costs

problem.claim: Unconstrained submodular maximization with modular costs models subset-selection profit maximization in applications including web mining, recommendation, and machine learning.

gap.claim: Worst-case approximation ratios for this NP-hard problem can be too pessimistic for evaluating approximate algorithms on real-world instances.

contributions.claim: The Monotone Surrogate Method is a unified framework for constructing data-dependent upper bounds for unconstrained submodular maximization with modular costs from bounds for monotone submodular maximization with a knapsack constraint.
The MSM+IP upper bound uses Iterative Prune and is no larger than the vanilla MSM upper bound.
Stability Interval tightening exploits intervals of the penalty parameter in which the IP-generated sublattice remains invariant.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across eight web-based applications, MSM+IP+SI consistently produced tighter data-dependent upper bounds than prior baselines.
The resulting empirical approximation ratios were far above the classic 1/3 ratio of double greedy and were often close to 0.9.

narrative_sequence.summary: Subset-selection profit maximization is modeled as unconstrained submodular maximization with modular costs.
Existing worst-case approximation ratios may poorly reflect performance on real-world instances.
The paper constructs data-dependent upper bounds and empirical approximation ratios through MSM.
MSM+IP and Stability Interval mechanisms further tighten the upper bound.
Experiments on eight web-based applications report tighter bounds and empirical ratios often near 0.9.

source_observation.claim: Data-dependent upper bounds can support empirical approximation ratios based on an algorithm's solution value.

interpretation.claim: Instance-specific evaluation may be more informative than a pessimistic worst-case ratio.

application.claim: Use data-dependent bounds to assess solution quality when worst-case guarantees do not discriminate among practical instances.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how tight or reliable these bounds are beyond the reported applications and experiments.

source_observation.claim: The bound can be tightened when the penalty parameter varies within a Stability Interval that leaves the generated sublattice unchanged.

interpretation.claim: Recognizing parameter regions with invariant intermediate structure can enable additional instance-specific tightening.

application.claim: Inspect parameter stability when refining data-dependent bounds for parameterized optimization problems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how Stability Intervals are computed or how broadly the technique generalizes.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide algorithmic details or computational complexity.
The abstract does not identify the eight applications, datasets, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide formal definitions or proof details for the bounds and Stability Interval.
